subject: Hosted API cost hypothesis + peak throughput sanity check
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.inference>
To: Aditi Sharma <aditi@novacorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-09-20T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API cost hypothesis + peak throughput sanity check

Hi Aditi —

Thanks for the chat today. Quick recap and the hypotheses we discussed so the team is aligned:

1) Expected monthly token footprint
- Your current pilot uses mostly short assistant responses (~40–80 tokens output) and some longer report generations (~600–1,200 tokens).
- Working hypothesis: steady-state monthly tokens = 10,000,000 – 14,000,000 tokens (10–14M).

2) Budget and unit economics target
- You mentioned a procurement budget range of roughly $10k–$16k / month for inference.
- Implied target unit price: approximately $1,000 – $1,600 per 1M tokens (depends on final SLA and burst needs).

3) Peak throughput (hosted API)
- Expected normal peak: ~350 tokens/sec (sustained few minutes).
- Short flash spikes during peak traffic up to ~900 tokens/sec (3–5 minutes).
- For requests-per-second framing: typical interactive workload ~2–4 rps; larger batch report jobs can push token TPS higher for short windows.

4) Latency & SLOs
- Target P95 generation latency <= 400ms for interactive flows; higher for report jobs is ok if batched.

Next steps we agreed on:
- I attached a simple MVP_pricing_model.xlsx showing how the budget range maps to $/1M token tiers and a draft SLA (SLA-draft.pdf).
- If the $/1M target range above looks reasonable, we can return a hosted pricing band and a 30-day proof-of-concept (metered) to validate real token velocity.
- Please share procurement contact and any PO timelines.

If any of the assumptions above are off, call them out and I’ll update the model.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MVP_pricing_model.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet) — high-level unit economics; SLA-draft.pdf (pdf) — initial SLA language
From: Aditi Sharma <aditi@novacorp.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.inference>
Cc: procurements@novacorp.com
Date: 2027-09-21T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API cost hypothesis + peak throughput sanity check

Thanks for the clear recap, Logan. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 10–14M monthly token estimate lines up with our internal instrumented run-rate for the use cases we showed. Good to double-check sample sizes in POC.
- Procurement asked whether the $/1M range you listed is list-pricing or expected after any volume discount. For our budget planning they need a conservative number. Can you provide two price bands: list and committed (12M/mo)?
- Peak TPS: the 900 tokens/sec spike sounds reasonable. For procurement/sre we need an estimate of concurrent requests during that spike (we have some parallel workers that will fan out). Can you convert the token TPS spike into requests-per-second assumptions for 3 profile types (short chat, medium assistant, long report)?

Also: procurement would like to see the draft SLA and a stub SOW for a 30-day POC that includes data handling notes (we're in healthcare vertical so audit & retention matter).

Best,
Aditi
Head of Product, Novacorp
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.inference>
To: Aditi Sharma <aditi@novacorp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, procurements@novacorp.com
Date: 2027-09-21T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API cost hypothesis + peak throughput sanity check

Aditi — thanks, good questions. Answers below and I’ve updated the attached MVP_pricing_model.xlsx with two bands: list vs committed for a 12M monthly commitment. Summary: 

Pricing bands (high level)
- List band: $1,600 per 1M tokens (no commit)
- Committed 12M/mo band: $1,050 per 1M tokens (12-month term)
- Example math: at 12M tokens/month a committed price of $1,050/1M → $12,600/month.

Requests-per-second mapping (assumptions)
- Short chat (average 60 tokens/response): 900 tokens/sec → ~15 rps.
- Medium assistant (average 300 tokens/response): 900 tokens/sec → ~3 rps.
- Long report (average 1,000 tokens/response): 900 tokens/sec → ~0.9 rps.

SLA / POC / compliance
- SLA-draft.pdf attached includes uptime targets and incident response windows; draft SOW for a 30-day metered POC is in the Drive link.
- For healthcare concerns: we support Private deployments (VPC) and can offer restricted logs with configurable retention for the POC; we’ll include the standard SOC2 artifacts and a short questionnaire response.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll upload the updated pricing band to the HubSpot deal (linked).
2) If Novacorp is comfortable, procurement can confirm whether they want list-pricing POC or committed POC (12M). If committed, we’ll prepare a simple MSA + SOW and timeboxed credits.
3) Please introduce procurement contact if different from the cc.

I’ll follow up with a short calendar invite for a procurement + SRE sync if helpful.

—
Logan
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: 2027-09-22T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Hosted API cost hypothesis + peak throughput sanity check

Quick internal note: if marketing/finance asks, recommended play: offer a one-time 8% on the committed 12M band (reduces $1,050 → $966/1M) for customers in healthcare with a 12-month MSA. Keeps list intact and helps procurement. Also flag privacy appendix for the POC (Marissa can draft).

Neha

Redwood Inference
